defense_analyst.prose: LA's defense is strong on third down, allowing conversions on 31.6% of attempts [dc1] over 114 plays [dc2], which ranks 4th in the league [dc3]. The softer spot is the red zone, where opponents have scored touchdowns on 46.4% of drives that reached the 20 [dc4], but that is a small sample of 28 drives [dc5]. Expect ARI's third-and-medium drives to be the hardest to sustain. Pressure is moderate rather than extreme: the pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) sits at 11.7% of dropbacks [dc6] over 326 dropbacks [dc7], with a 28.8% blitz rate [dc8] and 4.4 pass rushers per dropback [dc9], and a 4.9% sack rate [dc10]. Against the run, LA allows -0.18 EPA per carry [dc11] over 217 runs [dc12]. The pass defense allows explosive plays on 7.1% of pass plays [dc13] over 326 plays [dc14] and -0.07 EPA per pass [dc15]. Overall LA allows a 40.1% success rate [dc16] over 543 plays [dc17], ranked 4th in EPA allowed [dc18]. ARI's offense has been well below that level, with -0.04 EPA per play [dc19] ranking 21st of 32 [dc20] and a 43.3% success rate [dc21] over 600 plays [dc22]. The game plan should prioritize early-down success to avoid third-and-long against a front that can get home, and should be realistic that LA's defense is one of the league's better units.
